newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turk Cypriots shoot Greek Cypriot near U.N. zone.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cypriots shoot Greek Cypriot near U.N. zone.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot forces on Sunday shot a Greek Cypriot in civilian clothes who had crossed into Turkish Cypriot territory through the U.N. buffer zone dividing the island, Turkish Cypriot security officials said.
A Turkish Cypriot official told Reuters the incident happened at 0735 (0435 GMT) near the eastern end of the zone. He did not specify the medical condition of the Greek Cypriot.

"Turkish Cypriot forces on the spot challenged him three times, calling on him to stop. He did not. Three warning shots were fired into the area. He attempted to escape. Shots were fired and he was hit," the official said.
The shooting occurred near where a Turkish Cypriot soldier was shot dead close to the buffer zone last month, he said.
The official said the Greek Cypriot had "passed through the buffer zone and intruded on (Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus) TRNC territory".
A U.N spokesman was not immediately available for comment.

Tension on the Mediterranean island has increased since two Greek Cypriots were killed by Turks in incidents along the buffer zone in August. Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 following a Greek-engineered coup attempt on the island.
A Turkish Cypriot state in the north, recognised only by Ankara, was established in 1983.

A group of Greek Cypriot refugees from the 1974 fighting were set to hold a demonstration on western end of the buffer zone on Sunday to claim the right to return to their homes, now in the Turkish Cypriot area, Greek Cypriot radio said.
